odrive-botwheel.price: $120.00 (motor only); $260.00 with ZLAC8015 driver; $390.00 two motors with ZLAC8015D
odrive-botwheel.changes: The mount changes completely. It has a single-sided cantilever axle with an M16x1.5 thread and 12 mm flats (43 mm long), held by a nut through a slotted plate, instead of the BotWheel flange taking 4 x M6 on a 36 mm circle, so the wheel mount at the foot of the leg must be redrawn. Tyre is 173 ±2 mm dia x 44 mm wide (BotWheel 171 mm), overall width 118.2 mm. Mass is 3.75 kg vs 2.2 kg, i.e. +1.55 kg at each leg tip, which eats into the leg torque budget and needs the balance controller retuned. It has a 4096-line encoder and 15 pole pairs (BotWheel: hall + 3200 CPR), and ZLTECH power and signal connectors instead of JST PUD, so the ODrive harness must be re-terminated and its encoder and pole-pair settings changed; the alternative is ZLTECH's ZLAC8015D driver, which needs different firmware. It is 24 V, 6 N·m rated / 18 N·m peak, 160 rpm rated, IP65.
odrive-botwheel.evidence: Shopify .js variants and spec table (24 VDC, 350 W, 6 N·m rated, 18 N·m peak, 160 rpm rated, 205 rpm max, 4096 lines, 15 pole pairs, 3.75 kg, IP65, compatible driver ZLAC8015/ZLAC8015D). Tyre and axle dimensions read from the listing's linked drawing ZLLG65ASM250-4096_V2.0_-Drawing.pdf: Φ173 ±2, 118.2 ±0.5, 44 ±1, 43 ±0.3, M16x1.5, 12 flats.
